# Gijjhajātaka (Ja 427)

**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
In the text and commentary edited by V. Fausböll, it forms the first story of the *Navakanipāta*, immediately following the close of the *Aṭṭhanipāta* [Fausböll 1883]. The framing narrative (*paccuppannavatthu*) is set at Jetavana near Sāvatthī and was spoken by the Buddha concerning an unruly or disobedient monk (*dubbaca bhikkhu*) who failed to heed the admonitions and instructions of his teachers, preceptors, and companions in the holy life regarding monastic deportment [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883]. The opening verse incipit is recorded as *Parisamkupatho nāmā 'ti* (“Formed of rough logs...”) [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883].
Textual analysis conducted by DharmaNexus indicates substantial internal reuse with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Tatiyo bhāgo), matching extensive segments of the text (§1.1–9.6) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus identifies significant verse reuse between the *Gijjhajātaka* (§7.3–10.1) and another story concerning an unruly vulture, the *Migālopajātaka* (Ja 381, §4.4–7.1) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects cross-language alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155-2) [DharmaNexus].

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Tatiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a3) (§1.1–9.6 ↔ §4304–4332); Migālopajātaka (Ja 381) (§7.3–10.1 ↔ §4.4–7.1)
